method: Flesch-Kincaid grade with a transparent vowel-group syllable heuristic; estimated age = grade + 5, floored at zero. Count sentences using terminal punctuation. Exact measured corpora included. This is a rough editorial screen, not a learner assessment. Teacher-only text excluded.

corpora.text: I can try our story and choose one change. I can rehearse my own part. I can choose one cue or pose to change. I can keep my choice in my arts log. Find our story plan if it is here. Choose act, sit, stay silent or direct. Keep your own clear space. Use the open-hand stop cue. First: We want a den. Next: The space is small. Last: We choose a small den. Show the part you will do. Watch the same story twice. First, I rush the last cue. Next, I wait until all are ready. I change just one thing. Which cue is clear? Try our three parts once. A watcher says: I saw ___. Choose one cue or pose to change. Try that part again. Keep it or try once more. Rehearse your part with the group. Keep first, next and last. Test one change in a cue or pose. Ask a watcher what they saw. In your book or arts log, keep your own choice. Tell a watcher what you changed. Watcher: I saw ___. Choose one thing to keep. Relax and store your plan. My role was ___. I tried changing ___. The watcher saw ___. Next time I will ___. Try your part before the show. Make one part more clear. A sign to start or change. What a watcher saw or heard.

Use the three den story parts. Choose a role with the adult. Pick one cue or pose to change. Try it with help. Point to your own choice for your log. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Rehearse the three parts in order. Ask a watcher what they saw. Choose and test one change. Keep the feedback and your own part. Say what to try next. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use the same three-part task. Try two ways to give one cue. Ask which helps the group most. Choose one and say why. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

The group point to a wide space. Their hands move close to show a small space. The director waits until all are ready, then points to the word Start. The group show a small den. Each still pose lasts three comfortable seconds. What does the director check? How does the cue help the group? The group try the same three parts. A watcher cannot see the last pose. The group turn their hands towards the watcher and try again. The watcher sees a small roof. The story order stays the same. What did the group change? How could we check our end pose? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Show wide hands, close hands and a small roof. Say: First, next, last. Give the last cue before the model is ready. Say: That cue was too soon. Repeat. Check readiness and give one calm cue. Hold at most three comfortable seconds. Ask: Which ending could you follow? Keep the watcher's actual reply and name the one change. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Rehearse and refine our performance. I can rehearse my own part. I can choose one cue or pose to change. I can keep my choice in my arts log. rehearse: Try your part before the show. refine: Make one part more clear. cue: A sign to start or change. feedback: What a watcher saw or heard. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can use a real comment to make one part clear. I can rehearse the three parts. I can test one change from a real comment. I can name my role and next step for the show. Find our plan and real watcher note. Choose your role again. A fresh trial is fine if work is missing. Use clear space and the stop cue. Read or hear one real comment. What did the watcher see? Pick one part to try again. Say: We can change ___. Watch the end pose face away. A watcher says what they see. I turn the pose towards them. I try it again and ask once more. I keep the story order. Agree one change from our real note. Rehearse it once. The watcher says what is clear. Keep the change or try again. Agree our start and stop cues. Rehearse the story with your change. Keep your own role and safe space. Ask one watcher what they see now. Agree your role and cue for next week. In your arts log, keep the change and next step. What did our change help? What still needs a try? Check each person knows their cue. Store the plan for next week. The real comment was ___. We changed ___. It helped or needs more work because ___. My role and cue next time are ___. Make one part more clear. Try your part before the show. A person who watches. Set to start when the cue comes.

Hear one real watcher note. Pick a cue or pose to change. Try the story with the adult. Choose your role and cue for next time. Point to what changed for your log. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use real feedback to choose one change. Rehearse and check what the watcher sees. Keep or change the tested feature. Agree your role and cues for next week. Log your own part and next step. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same rehearsal task. Compare the first and later trial. Say how one change helped the viewer. Choose one small check before the show. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Show a small roof pose facing away. Ask what the watcher can see. Use the actual reply. Say: I will turn the pose towards you. Repeat the same end pose facing the watcher. Freeze for at most three comfortable seconds. Ask what is clear now. Say: I keep this change if it helps. Next week is the show. Choose your role. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

I can rehearse our scene and choose one clear target. I can play or direct my agreed role. I can use a real trial to choose one change. I can log my own choice and the viewer's response. Find our scene plan if it is here. Choose an actor, seated, silent or director role. Keep your own clear space. Use the agreed stop cue. Recall plan, change, choice and result. What is your own part? Which part needs a clearer cue? Keep any real feedback from last week. Watch two trials of one transition. First, the cue comes before all are ready. Next, the director checks and gives one cue. The story stays the same. What does the viewer see now? Run our four beats once. Ask: Which part was hard to follow? Choose one target as a group. Try that part again. Keep the viewer's real comment. Rehearse a short scene of about 30 to 60 seconds. Keep plan, change, choice and result. Test one target in a second trial. Ask a class or staff viewer what they saw. In your arts log, keep your own part and the result. What did the viewer understand? Which change will we keep? What still needs a try? Store the plan and notes for Wednesday. My role and choice were ___. Our target was ___. We tried ___, then ___. The viewer noticed ___. Next time I will ___. Practise a scene before the show. Make a chosen part clearer. The move from one story beat to the next. One thing we choose to improve.

Use the four-beat story with staff help. Choose a role and one feature to test. Try the scene twice in a safe way. Ask a viewer what they saw. Confirm your own choice for the log. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Run the four-beat scene once. Choose one target from a real response. Rehearse with one change. Check the viewer's understanding. Log your part, choice and next step. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same scene and log. Compare the first and later trial. Link one feature to what the viewer saw. Choose a clear check for the next rehearsal. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

A group rehearse plan, change, choice and result. The first cue comes before everyone is ready. In the next trial, a cue keeper checks each role, points to the word Start, then starts. The group begin the new small move together. Which part changes in the second trial? How can we test whether a cue helps? A group show wide moves, a smaller space, a choice and a new small move. A viewer misses the choice. The group add a quiet pause before asking What could we try? The viewer now notices that the group make a new plan. What did the viewer miss at first? How might a pause make our choice beat clear? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Name plan, change, choice and result. Show the transition into the small move. Give a cue too soon in the adult model. Ask which part was hard to follow. Try a short scene. Change one thing. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Choose one skill in your role. Compare your first and later trial. What changed? What did the viewer see? Set one small skill goal for Wednesday. Keep your own choice, both real trial notes and the viewer's words. Add your skill goal and how you will check it.
